text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash accepts President Glafcos Clerides's proposal for demilitarisation talks, with preconditions.
- Four Israelis involved in bungled escape bid are remanded for four days.
- The British bases have no indication of who killed a Turkish Cypriot sentry at his post close to the buffer zone on Sunday.
- Police say mental patient confessed to hospital killings.
- Involvement of Turkish officials in Dherinia murder can't just be washed away, says Clerides in his letter to Denktash.
- Two years since the brutal murder of a Danish tour guide, the British army has tried to clean up its image.
- Clerides agrees to a meeting with Denktash, but with conditions.
- Yugoslavian is found dead from a heroin overdose.
- Cyprus Airways chairman Vassilis Rologis is to quit company after his election as president of the Cyprus Chamber of Commerce and Industry.
- Satanic killer is found in the psychiatric hospital. "They were a burden on society," he says of his two victims.
- Teachers union warns it will not send its members to teach at primary schools with less than 15 teachers.
- The government looks set to review draft legislation banning strikes in essential sectors after dockworkers strike in Limassol port.
